name: Agriculture and agro-processing
summary: Coffee export earnings reached a record 3 billion USD in the budget year that ended in July 2026, and agriculture accounted for 32.8 percent of Ethiopia's GDP and 60.1 percent of employment in 2025 (World Bank). The Ethiopian Investment Commission promotes agro-processing in edible oil, juices, animal feed, tomato and poultry, where large shares of demand are currently met by imports, and integrated agro-industrial parks offer ready-made sheds with income and export tax exemptions. FAO-hosted investment cases presented in 2025 and 2026 project internal rates of return of 20.8 to 32 percent for animal feed, ranching, poultry and coffee projects.

opportunities.title: Edible oil processing
opportunities.detail: Edible oil demand is above 850,000 MT against 550,000 MT of supply, with 95 percent of supply imported at over US$650 million per year; EIC lists sesame, soybean, niger seed, groundnut and linseed processing.

opportunities.title: Animal feed and poultry
opportunities.detail: EIC cites US$150 million of unmet domestic demand for animal feed. An FAO-hosted 2026 investment case for animal feed projects an IRR of 20.8 percent.

opportunities.title: Coffee processing and rejuvenation
opportunities.detail: FAO-hosted 2025 investment cases propose dry and wet coffee processing factories (USD 164.4 million and USD 97.2 million) and coffee rejuvenation, with projected IRRs of 30 and 32 percent.

opportunities.title: Integrated agro-industrial parks
opportunities.detail: Parks at Burie, Yirgalem and Bulbula offer ready-made sheds of 1,500 to 3,500 square meters at US$1.5 per square meter per month for foreign investors, and power at US$0.045/kWh.

opportunities.title: Tomato and tropical fruit processing
opportunities.detail: Processed tomato demand is growing 15 percent per year with 55 percent imported, and the local tropical juice market is over US$100 million, 40 percent unmet.

opportunities.title: Livestock-based industries and leather inputs
opportunities.detail: EIC lists 65,354,092 cows, 50,243,044 goats and 39,894,394 sheep and promotes animal ranches and the tanning of hides and skins.

incentives.detail: Integrated agro-industrial park investors get completed infrastructure, income tax exemption, export tax exemption, streamlined and expedited procedures, and access to an Export Credit Guarantee Scheme.
Exemption from duties and other taxes on imports of machinery, equipment and construction material (also spare parts, raw materials and vehicles), plus a duty-free privilege for exporters.
Up to 10 years income-tax holiday for enterprises producing inside industrial parks.
The World Bank reports a significant increase in agricultural machinery imports in FY26 that benefited from import duty waivers and forex availability.

risks.detail: Access to finance: UNIDO estimates the coffee value chain's overall financing gap at 95 percent, with loan interest rates of 18-30 percent, so financing structure is a key part of project planning.

Farm productivity: about 80 percent of coffee trees are 50-70 years old and adoption of good agricultural practices is low, and climate, pests and diseases need active management; the coffee rejuvenation investment case above targets this replanting need.

Input and operating factors: FAO-hosted investment cases point to raw material supply consistency and price movements for feed, climate and land suitability for ranching, and capital costs, foreign exchange access and animal health for poultry.

Export finance: the World Bank notes that bank liquidity and lending limits affect exporters' ability to finance international orders, particularly for smaller exporters; the same project document reports improved forex availability in FY26.
